annotations.text:
AITutor — a per-course study space.

Row 1: getting in and setting up.  Row 2: the spine — a course, a session, a question.  Row 3: the study loop — write, get checked, practise, see where you stand.  Row 4: the phone.

Warm paper, ink text, one deep-teal accent that only ever means "you can press this" or "this is a citation". Static mockups, not a clickable prototype.

The citation carries the same visual weight as the sentence it supports, and opening it puts the actual slide beside the answer. The exchange above shows the other required outcome: "your material doesn't cover this", said plainly, with what appears to be missing.

Deliberately blank. No slides, no outline, no previous summary — anything shown here would let the student assemble instead of recall, and recall is the whole mechanism. The note at the bottom explains the emptiness so it doesn't read as broken.

Untouched objectives sort first and are the largest thing on the page; the ones already worked on collapse to a quiet list at the bottom. Gaps read as unfilled, never as red — a gap is information, not a telling-off.

Capture is the one flow that has to work in a corridor on a bad connection: 52px targets, offline banner, and writing your own account is always invited and never required. No fake OS status bar — the real one renders on top.
